item.statement: nu product neurons with phases alpha_l = pi l/nu produce table nu lambda^nu 2^{-n} cos(2 pi j(sum a - c)/p), norm nu lambda^2 p/2 each; one block per support frequency attains the class value
item.what_to_check: Compare constructions in Morwani, Gromov 2023, Li et al. 2025, Nanda; trig/roots-of-unity cancellation

chk.evidence:
The trigonometric identity behind the nu-block is classical. Mohlenkamp and Monzón, "Trigonometric identities and sums of separable functions", Math. Intelligencer 27(2):65-69 (2005), DOI 10.1007/BF02985795 (metadata confirmed via Crossref; preprint read at ohiouniversityfaculty.com/mohlenka/research/sine.pdf). Their Thm 2 gives sin(sum_{j=1}^n x_j) = sum_j sin(x_j) prod_{k!=j} sin(x_k+alpha_k-alpha_j)/sin(alpha_k-alpha_j) for any distinct alpha, together with a shifted version with free a_j (sum a_j = 0). They state that sin of a sum "is exactly separated with separation rank n", compared with 2^{n-1} terms from the standard trig expansion. Their Fig. 1 (right) uses equally spaced alpha = 0, pi/3, 2pi/3. Minimality is only conjectured ("We believe..."). I checked numerically that the choice alpha_k = pi k/nu, a_k = -alpha_k, together with prod_{k=1}^{nu-1} sin(pi k/nu) = nu/2^{nu-1}, gives exactly our identity sum_{l=0}^{nu-1} (-1)^l prod_{k=1}^{nu} cos(x_k + pi l/nu) = nu 2^{1-nu} cos(sum x_k). This matches for nu = 2..7, and our block is that identity with x_nu = -theta_c.

None of the ML constructions uses a nu-neuron roots-of-unity block:
- Morwani et al. ICLR 2024, App. F.2 (PDF read): 8 neurons per frequency. They expand cos(a+b-c) into 4 trig terms and implement each with a neuron pair, with phases (0,0,0)/(0,pi,pi), (pi/2,-pi/2,0)/(pi/2,pi/2,pi) and so on. They credit Gromov's scheme.
- Li, Liang, Shi, Song, Zhou, AISTATS 2025, Lemma E.1 Part 3 and Lemma E.2/E.3: 2^{2k-1} neurons per frequency pair, built by sign-vector polarisation of 2^k trig terms. No roots-of-unity phases.
- Gromov 2023 (arXiv 2301.02679), Eqs. 6-16: random uniform phases with phi1+phi2=phi3. Spurious terms cancel only approximately (the random phase approximation). Doshi, He, Das, Gromov 2024 (arXiv 2406.03495), Eq. 2 is the same random-phase scheme for S-term sums.
- He, Wang, Chen, Yang (arXiv 2602.16849), Def 4.1(iii): phase-moment cancellation for iota in {2,4} within each frequency group (roots of unity satisfy it). Their setting is quadratic sum-activation nets, where noise peaks at 2x and 2y survive (Prop 4.2). There is no minimal block and no norm optimality.

The roots-of-unity filter itself is the textbook series-multisection identity.

What remains ours: the product-network norm accounting (nu lambda^2 p/2), the amplitude weighting lambda_j^nu = 2^n y*_j/nu, and the result that one block per support frequency attains Gamma_s. Cost-optimality of nu neurons is the separate lem:cost; the minimal-rank question is only conjectured in Mohlenkamp and Monzón.

Searches run: PDFs of Morwani, Li, Gromov, Doshi and He et al. grepped for their constructions and phases; web search for Mohlenkamp and Monzón; web search for the tensor rank of sin(x1+...+xd) (no minimality proof found). recommended_citations.why: Supports prop:block's identity. Thm 2 writes sin of a sum of n variables as n separable terms using phase parameters alpha_j, instead of the 2^{n-1} terms of the standard expansion. With equally spaced alpha = pi k/nu and shifts, it reduces exactly to our nu-block table identity. It should be cited as the source of the 'nu neurons suffice' identity.
App. F.2 gives the max-margin quadratic construction with 8 neurons per frequency (a trig expansion plus sign-pair neurons). Cite it as a contrast when introducing the block.
Lemma E.3 builds the k-sum max-margin network with 2^{2k-1} neurons per frequency pair, using Lemma E.1 sign polarisation. Cite it as a contrast: exponential versus our nu neurons per frequency.
Eqs. 6-16 use the analytic phases phi1+phi2=phi3 with random phases, so spurious terms cancel only approximately. Our phases make the same cancellation exact.

Def 4.1(iii) is a phase-moment cancellation condition, which roots-of-unity phases satisfy, found in trained quadratic nets. Cite it for the phase-symmetry intuition near the sentence 'The phases are a rotated copy of the nu-th roots of unity'.

chk.recommended_change: In cyclic.tex, after prop:block (the sentence "The phases are a rotated copy of the nu-th roots of unity..."), add: "The table identity is the equally spaced case of the nu-term separable expansion of the sine of a sum \citep{mohlenkamp2005trig} (their Thm 2, which replaces the 2^{nu-1} terms of the standard expansion by nu). Earlier max-margin constructions use 8 neurons per frequency \citep[App. F]{morwani2024feature} and 2^{2k-1} for k summands \citep[Lemma E.3]{li2025nsum}. Random-phase constructions cancel only approximately \citep{gromov2023grokking}. What is new here is the weighting lambda_j^nu proportional to y*_j and the fact that these blocks attain Gamma_s (and, by Lemma cost, are cost-optimal)." Do not present the roots-of-unity cancellation itself as new. Mohlenkamp and Monzón only conjecture minimality of rank n, so our cost lemma is not pre-empted by them.
